item.title: In Riyadh, a Houthi missile damages the tower of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund
item.description:
The Public Investment Fund tower, Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper, was hit before dawn on Thursday, with no casualties according to civil defence. The Saudi-led coalition is stepping up its strikes in Yemen.

A missile fired by the Houthis damaged the 80-storey tower of the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund, in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District before dawn on Thursday November 19th, blowing out windows on seven or eight floors but injuring no one, according to civil defence. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted four ballistic missiles and a cruise missile aimed at the south of the kingdom and destroyed a launcher in Saada province; it was the second hit on the financial district in under two weeks, after an Aramco building on November 8th. The Houthis say Saudi strikes have killed ten people in Sanaa in two days, while Yemen’s Presidential Council has designated them a "terrorist" organisation and Donald Trump says he wants to see "what happens after January 1st" with Iran.

item.title: Houthi attack damages an Aramco tower in the heart of Riyadh’s financial district
item.description:
Missiles fired from Yemen were intercepted over the Saudi capital on Sunday, but debris struck a building belonging to the oil giant. The Houthi authorities accuse Saudi aircraft of killing dozens of people near Sanaa.

Overnight on Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh, but debris blew out the windows of several floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District, causing no casualties, according to the energy ministry. The Iran-aligned Yemeni rebels have stepped up their fire on the kingdom’s ports and airports since September, and their spokesman, Yahya Saree, claims they also targeted Riyadh’s international airport, which the Saudi authorities have not confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed missile launchers in Saada and Sanaa, while the Houthi-run health ministry reports at least 33 people killed on Saturday and 40 on Sunday in Saudi strikes near the Yemeni capital.
